argument.notes: Projection does not increase Euclidean diameter. Enlarging the bounded vertical projections produces measurable interval majorants with total weighted error at most epsilon. Every horizontal slice is covered by the corresponding first-coordinate projections, so the content infimum gives the pointwise lower bound. Integration over the unit interval and M001 give c≤sum rho_i^(s+1)+epsilon. The infinite-cost branch and the finite-cost epsilon argument are both valid; taking the infimum over all covers proves N004. Empty members and zero diameters are handled, and no measurability of the original covering sets is used.

background_notes.fact: If V is a nonempty subset of Eucl(n)×R with finite diameter rho, both coordinate projections are nonempty and have diameter at most rho. Its last-coordinate image B is bounded and has real infimum and supremum with sup B−inf B≤rho.

background_notes.justification: Each coordinate distance is at most the product distance. Taking suprema of pairwise distances proves the diameter bounds. Fixing one point of B bounds every other point within rho. Real completeness supplies its infimum and supremum. From b≤b'+rho for all b,b'∈B, taking first the infimum in b' and then the supremum in b gives sup B≤inf B+rho.

background_notes.fact: For a nonempty bounded B⊆R of span at most rho and eta>0, J=(inf B−eta/2,sup B+eta/2) is bounded, open and contains B, with lambda(J∩I)≤rho+eta. For T⊆N and eta_i=epsilon 2^(−i−1)/(1+rho_i^s), sum_{i∈T} eta_i rho_i^s≤epsilon.

background_notes.justification: The strict endpoint enlargement contains every point of B even for span zero. Interval length equals span+eta, and measure monotonicity bounds its intersection with I. Each weighted eta_i is at most epsilon 2^(−i−1). The first m geometric weights sum to 1−2^(−m); their supremum is 1, since 2^(−m) tends to zero. Every finite subfamily of T is contained in an initial segment of N, so its geometric sum is at most 1; taking the supremum over finite subfamilies proves the claimed series bound.

background_notes.fact: For s>0, the map r↦r^s is increasing on nonnegative real numbers, has 0^s=0, and finite input gives finite output. Thus a countable delta-cover with diameters bounded by rho_i has s-cost at most sum rho_i^s. A constant nonnegative coefficient times an indicator of an open subset of R is Borel measurable and hence almost-everywhere measurable for any measure on this Borel space.

background_notes.justification: The nonnegative integral is defined by measurable simple functions below the integrand. This directly makes it monotone and gives the indicator formula; constant functions are the special case J=R. The measure outside I under the restriction is zero, so the pointwise inequality on I is an almost-everywhere inequality. The countable sum is measurable as the increasing limit of its measurable finite partial sums. Thus monotonicity applies before the explicit M001 interchange.

background_notes.fact: Nonnegative countable series permit termwise comparison and satisfy sum_i(a_i+b_i)=sum_i a_i+sum_i b_i in [0,infinity], without summability assumptions. For finite rho≥0 and s>0, rho^s rho=rho^(s+1), including rho=0.

grounds.reason: rho_i are finite and nonnegative.
The interval measure bounds and weighted error series bound are available.

background_notes.justification: A nonnegative countable sum is the supremum of its finite subsums, which gives comparison. Finite distributivity followed by suprema gives addition of the series: finite subsums of two families can be bounded together using the union of their finite index sets. For rho>0 the power identity follows from exp((s+1) log rho)=exp(s log rho)rho; for rho=0 both powers vanish since both exponents are positive.

background_notes.fact: If finite c≥0 and K∈[0,infinity] satisfy c≤K+e for every real e>0, then c≤K.

background_notes.justification: For K=infinity the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise K is real; if c>K, choose e=(c−K)/2>0, contradicting c≤K+e. No exchange of limits, covers or integrals is involved.

background_notes.fact: If c∈[0,infinity] is a lower bound for the costs of all admissible covers, then c is at most their infimum, with the infimum of no costs equal to infinity. Deleting empty members or padding with empty sets preserves a positive-exponent countable cover cost.

background_notes.justification: The infimum is the greatest lower bound in the complete ordered set [0,infinity]; hence every lower bound lies below it, also for an empty family. Countable families admit natural-number indexing with empty padding (finite and empty families included); empty contributions are zero and do not change a nonnegative sum.
